subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: continuously measures what is happening in the city.
parts: traffic loop detectors and camera-based counting

subsystems.name: Data integration layer
subsystems.role: turns many incompatible feeds and static datasets into one consistent, queryable model.

subsystems.name: City model repository
subsystems.role: stores the 3D geometry and attributes of buildings, streets, networks and terrain.
parts: building models (BIM/IFC, CityGML levels of detail)

subsystems.name: Simulation and analytics engine
subsystems.role: replays and predicts how the city behaves.

subsystems.name: Visualisation and decision interface
subsystems.role: makes the model usable by planners, operators and the public.

subsystems.name: Governance and actuation layer
subsystems.role: decides what the twin is allowed to see, keep and change.

buildSteps.title: Decide what decisions the twin must support
buildSteps.detail: A twin is built backwards from questions — a congestion scheme, a heatwave plan, a new tram line — not from a wish for a pretty model.

buildSteps.title: Build the static 3D city
buildSteps.detail: Aerial LiDAR and photogrammetry flights capture rooftops and terrain; cadastral records give parcels; BIM models give new and large buildings. These are merged into a standards-based city model at an agreed level of detail.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the city
buildSteps.detail: Traffic counts, transit feeds, meters, air-quality stations and waste sensors are installed or, more often, existing ones are connected under data-sharing agreements.

buildSteps.title: Pipe the data in
buildSteps.detail: Feeds are streamed into a platform, cleaned, time-stamped and linked to the right building, road segment or substation using a common semantic model.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the models
buildSteps.detail: Traffic, energy and water models are tuned until replaying last year reproduces last year's measurements within an acceptable error.

buildSteps.title: Couple the domains
buildSteps.detail: Traffic affects air quality, which affects health, which affects energy demand. Interfaces let one model's output feed another, with agreed time steps.

buildSteps.title: Run scenarios and compare options
buildSteps.detail: Planners change one variable — a bus lane, a heat pump rollout, a new district — and read the modelled consequences across domains.

buildSteps.title: Move from what-if to operations
buildSteps.detail: The twin is connected to control rooms and real-time dashboards, with alerts when live conditions diverge from prediction.

buildSteps.title: Keep it alive
buildSteps.detail: Cities change constantly: re-survey, detect change automatically, retrain models and retire data that is no longer valid.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap, dense IoT sensing and low-power networks
prerequisites.why: a twin is only as good as the data flowing into it; LoRaWAN, NB-IoT and 5G make widespread metering and counting affordable.
CityGML, IFC and 3D Tiles let geometry from surveyors, architects and utilities coexist — though city data remains fragmented in practice.
continuous ingestion plus 3D rendering at city scale needs elastic compute that did not exist affordably a decade ago.
traffic and energy models work well individually, but coupled multi-domain models still carry large uncertainties.
twinning movement data risks surveillance; anonymisation and aggregation are improving but not standardised.

pathway.milestone: static and semi-live 3D city models used for planning and consultation
pathway.unlocks: shared visual understanding between engineers, officials and residents.

pathway.milestone: operational twins with live traffic, energy and environmental feeds in control rooms
pathway.unlocks: faster incident response and evidence-based day-to-day management.

pathway.milestone: coupled scenario twins, where planners test a policy across transport, energy and climate together
pathway.unlocks: fewer costly surprises from single-domain decisions.

pathway.milestone: federated twins linking neighbouring cities and regions under common standards
pathway.unlocks: regional planning for grids, floods and transport that no single city can do alone.
